# Status report: jf2 allocator test on kestrel, 2026-11-20

## Short version

On the read-mostly benchmark, the jf2 build (our fork of the jemalloc memory allocator) reduced the p99 latency of kestrel (our key-value store) by 59%, from 2140 us to 870 us. Throughput and median latency did not change measurably. The cost is 5.7 GB (9.3%) more memory, which needs approval from the capacity team, and the write-heavy workload is not tested yet.

## Words used here

- **Build A**: main@4f1c2aa with jemalloc 5.3, the current allocator.
- **Build B**: the same commit with jf2.
- **ycsb-b / ycsb-a**: two standard workloads of the YCSB database benchmark. ycsb-b is read-mostly and ycsb-a is write-heavy.
- **p50 / p99 / p99.9 latency**: the response time that 50% / 99% / 99.9% of requests stay under. p99 and p99.9 describe the slowest requests.
- **kops/s**: thousands of operations per second.
- **RSS**: resident set size, the physical memory the process holds.
- **Decay purge**: the allocator step that returns unused memory to the operating system after a delay.
- **perf**: the Linux sampling profiler.
- **logrotate**: a scheduled system job that rotates log files.
- **NUMA pinning**: binding the process to the CPUs and memory of one processor socket.

## Setup

- **Host:** bench-07, 2 x 32-core Xeon, 512 GB memory, kernel 6.8.
- **System load before the runs:** load average 0.4, which is close to idle on 64 cores.
- **Workload:** ycsb-b with 64 client threads, 10 minutes per run.
- **Runs:** 5 per build, alternating A, B, A, B, so that slow changes on the host affect both builds equally.

## Results

```
Latency, median of 5 runs. Lower is better. One block = 245 us.

p99    A  █████████  2140 us
       B  ████  870 us   (-59%)

p99.9  A  ████████████████████████████████████████  9800 us
       B  █████████████  3100 us   (-68%)
```

Only the latency of the slowest requests changed.

| Metric (median, min..max) | Build A | Build B | Change, B vs A |
|---|---|---|---|
| Throughput, kops/s | 412 (405..418) | 409 (401..415) | -3 (-0.7%), ranges overlap |
| p50 latency, us | 118 (116..121) | 119 (117..121) | +1 (+0.8%), ranges overlap |
| p99 latency, us | 2140 (1890..2610) | 870 (820..940) | -1270 (-59%), no overlap |
| p99.9 latency, us | 9800 (7200..14100) | 3100 (2700..3900) | -6700 (-68%), no overlap |
| RSS at end of run, GB | 61.2 | 66.9 | +5.7 (+9.3%) |

The notes give one RSS value per build, with no range.

## What the data shows

- **jf2 reduces the latency of the slowest requests on ycsb-b.** The worst B run is faster than the best A run for both p99 (940 us against 1890 us) and p99.9 (3900 us against 7200 us).
- **jf2 also makes that latency more stable.** The run-to-run range of p99 is 120 us for build B and 720 us for build A.
- **Throughput and median latency did not change measurably.** The medians differ by less than 1%, and the ranges of the two builds overlap.
- **The decay purge is the likely cause of the spikes in build A.** The spikes (short periods of much higher latency) occur at the same times as the purge. perf attributes 31% of the samples taken during spikes to `je_arena_decay`, the jemalloc purge function. jf2 does the purge in a background thread.
- **jf2 uses more memory.** RSS at the end of the run is 5.7 GB (9.3%) higher.

The notes do not state a target value for p99, so this report says "reduced" and not "fixed".

## Data quality note

Run 3 of build B had a 40 s stall at minute 7. The stall was traced to the nightly logrotate job, not to the allocator. The run was repeated, and the repeat replaces the stalled run in the build B numbers above.

Suggestion: disable the logrotate job on bench-07 during test runs, or schedule runs outside its time window.

## Not tested

- ycsb-a, the write-heavy workload.
- More than 64 client threads.
- NUMA pinning.

The results above apply only to ycsb-b with 64 threads and no pinning.

## Open decision

Is 5.7 GB (9.3%) more RSS acceptable? The capacity team must approve this.

## Next steps

1. Run ycsb-a on 2026-11-21.
2. Ask the capacity team for a decision on the RSS increase.
3. If the capacity team approves, enable jf2 behind a flag in staging.
